notes: The library's own news item states UM is 'investing in a partner subscription with OpenAlex' and that the partner status lets UM influence OpenAlex's development, including adding content relevant to UM; no fee figure is published (OpenAlex's public tiers are Member, Member+ and Partner). The same announcement pairs the subscription with ending Scopus. This is a confirmed paid open-infrastructure commitment that directly displaces spend on a commercial abstract and citation database.
signal: Maastricht University Library announced it is investing in a Partner-tier paid subscription with OpenAlex as part of a shift to open research information.

notes: TU Delft Library confirmed it is discontinuing its subscription to the Web of Science Core Collection and related databases, and published a transition guide pointing researchers to alternative resources. The library's Library4Research blog runs a dedicated OpenAlex tag and a June 2025 post promoting OpenAlex for TU Delft researchers, noting OpenAlex underpins the CWTS Leiden Ranking Open Edition. No paid OpenAlex Member/Member+/Partner subscription is disclosed on any TU Delft page surfaced.
signal: ACTIVE, NOT CONFIRMED PAYING. Web of Science Core Collection cancelled; library promotes OpenAlex as alternative.

This deepens Leiden's stake in OpenAlex's data quality and roadmap. Note: seen on a third-party page, not a Leiden or OurResearch page, so it should be verified with OurResearch before being used in a renewal argument.
signal: OpenAlex's Topics subject-classification system was developed in collaboration with Leiden University's Centre for Science and Technology Studies (CWTS).

notes: NWO's own 'Open science infrastructure support' page lists OpenAlex (run by non-profit OurResearch, also behind Unpaywall) among the open infrastructures it financially supports, stating a duration of 2024-2025 and an annual amount of 12,500 dollars. The amount is explicitly disclosed by the funder, but NWO describes it as infrastructure support and does not map it to any of OpenAlex's named Member/Member+/Partner tiers, so tier is left null. The same page lists comparable support for OpenCitations, indicating a portfolio approach to open metadata infrastructure rather than a single product subscription. No renewal beyond 2025 was found in this search.

notes: Utrecht University Library maintains a dedicated OpenAlex LibGuide describing OpenAlex as a free and open catalogue of the world's scholarly research system run by a non-profit, and directing users to contact the library for support. The university separately published a background interview with its open science specialist Jeroen Bosman assessing whether OpenAlex could replace expensive commercial subscriptions. No paid Member, Member+ or Partner subscription was found for Utrecht in this search, so status is active rather than subscriber.
signal: ACTIVE, UNPAID. Library runs a dedicated OpenAlex LibGuide; no paid subscription found.

notes: The University of Groningen library announced that access to Web of Science will end on 31 December 2026, and points users to alternatives including the open databases OpenAlex and The Lens. Importantly, the library names Scopus (retained) as the suitable alternative for systematic literature reviews and states that OpenAlex and The Lens are less suitable for that use case, so OpenAlex is a partial rather than full replacement. The announce date is taken from the library news item's own dated URL. No OpenAlex subscription or fee is mentioned, so no paid status is claimed.
signal: NO SUBSCRIPTION CONFIRMED. Web of Science ends 31 Dec 2026; OpenAlex named as an open alternative (Scopus retained).

notes: VU Amsterdam's University Library announced it will terminate its Clarivate Web of Science licence with effect from 1 January 2026, citing its commitment to the Barcelona Declaration on Open Research Information and the fact that Web of Science is a closed commercial system. The VU library's 'Search systems and reference tools' page lists OpenAlex as an open-source, freely accessible source of publication data offering citation, open-access and SDG indicators. No paid OpenAlex Member/Member+/Partner subscription is stated on either page, so this is engagement, not a confirmed contract.
signal: NO PAID TIER CONFIRMED. Cancelled Web of Science eff. 2026-01-01 on open-research-information grounds; OpenAlex listed as library search tool.

notes: University of Groningen Library news announced that the University of Groningen and the University Medical Centre Groningen will jointly cancel their Web of Science licence with effect from 1 January 2027, citing relatively high licence cost, functional overlap with retained databases, and a growing institutional commitment to open research information. UMCG is a separate legal entity from UG and is not currently a tracked record, so this is a net-new account rather than an update to the Groningen row. notes: ZonMw's own site states that it and NWO both signed the Barcelona Declaration published on 16 April 2024, committing to openness of bibliographic metadata as part of the wider open science movement. As a national health research funder, this makes open metadata (Crossref/OpenAlex-class sources) the default basis for its reporting and analysis. A funder mandate of this kind weakens the case for Scopus/Web of Science as the evidence base in Dutch grant monitoring and evaluation.

The same network post notes open research information is embedded in the new Strategy Evaluation Protocol 2027-2033, which directly reduces the evaluative need for closed citation databases.
